classification.difficultyReason: Translate a requirement for two distinct real roots into a parameter inequality and select its solution intervals using a parabola.

inlines.text: ; the upward parabola is positive outside its roots.

answer.worked:
Two distinct real roots require $\Delta>0$.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-k)^2-4(1)(4)\\\Delta&=k^2-16\end{align*}$$

Thus $k^2-16>0$. Find the boundary values:

$$\begin{align*}k^2-16&=0\\(k-4)(k+4)&=0\\k&=-4\text{ or }k=4\end{align*}$$

The sketch of $y=k^2-16$ opens upwards and lies above the $k$-axis outside these roots. At either boundary, $\Delta=0$, so both boundaries are excluded.

Hence $k<-4$ or $k>4$.
